title: Luckin Coffee — The Fraud Unravels
timebase: Integer timeline frames, 24 fps; segment timecode starts at 00:00:30:00 in the full film; local frame 0 equals full-film frame 720.
status: Storyboard and motion plan only. Do not treat this file as a completed animation or a sourced documentary edit.
voiceoverDraft: To understand what survived, first understand the SEC’s allegations. The SEC alleged that Luckin fabricated more than RMB 2.12 billion in retail sales from April 2019 through January 2020. Its complaint described three purchasing schemes involving related parties. It also said employees inflated expenses by more than $190 million, created a fake operations database, and altered accounting and bank records. The matter surfaced during the annual external audit. Luckin reported it and began an internal investigation. It later agreed to a $180 million SEC penalty without admitting or denying the charges. Nasdaq delisted the shares in July 2020. The ticker vanished. What happened to the coffee business?

researchGaps: The exact date and terms of the company’s public disclosure require a primary company filing citation before final narration.
The exact delisting date should be shown only after verifying the Nasdaq notice or an SEC/company filing; current narration uses July 2020 at month precision.
The next segment must source the operating business after delisting; this segment poses the question but does not claim recovery metrics.
accuracyRules: Attribute the fraud mechanics to the SEC complaint; use allegation wording, not an unsourced narration voice that states allegations as adjudicated findings.
All diagrams and record-like surfaces are illustrative; never fabricate receipt text, order IDs, account records, auditor marks, or company documents.
Settlement wording must preserve the SEC statement that Luckin agreed without admitting or denying the charges.
A delisting is not a business closure; do not imply that operations ended or recovered without separate sourcing.
